title_en: Fall 2026 Graduate Thesis Examination Schedule and Procedures
summary: Master's and doctoral students who meet the eligibility requirements and wish to undergo thesis examination in Fall 2026 must apply online on the department intranet and submit the application documents to the department office (Building 301, Room 319) between 21 September and 1 October 2026, 17:00. They must then pay the examination fee by 3 November 2026, 17:00, and submit result documents by 14 December 2026, 17:00 (master's) or 21 December 2026, 17:00 (doctoral). The final thesis must be uploaded to the library by 1 February 2027, 23:59, and the original approval page and confirmation form must be submitted to the department office by 22 January 2027, 17:00.
applies_to: Graduate students (master's and doctoral) of the department who wish to undergo thesis examination in Fall 2026. To apply, a student must: have passed the thesis qualifying examination (foreign language and major examination); meet the course completion requirements; meet the degree conferral (publication) requirements in force for Fall 2026; and, if they have already completed coursework, be registered as a graduate research student and still be within their thesis submission period (4 years after completion for master's, 6 years for doctoral; this period applies to completers only). Doctoral thesis examinations (first and final examination) are only for students who passed the preliminary examination last semester. Students who withdrew from thesis examination last semester must repeat every step from the online application. Thesis examination is not compulsory for all students; only those applying must follow these steps.

conditions: The content of this notice may change later; check it regularly.
Students taking the Fall 2026 thesis qualifying examination should apply first; if they fail it, they must contact the department office to cancel.
If a student fails the foreign language part, they cannot print the fee bill even if they passed the major examination.

Students not yet recognised as passing the English part must obtain a TEPS or TOEFL score at or above the College of Engineering threshold and submit it to the department office before submitting thesis examination documents.
The SNU completion simulator does not reflect department rules and is not accurate; students must check completion using the self-diagnosis checklist in the FAQ post and the academic handbook.
If completion requirements are not met, graduation is not possible regardless of whether the thesis examination is passed.

Abstract-only conference publications are recognised only if the conference has peer review; a confirmation form signed by the preliminary examination committee must be submitted before the result documents deadline (the signature may be obtained after the preliminary examination).

Master's publication requirement: at least one domestic or international conference or journal paper published or accepted, with the student as first author excluding the advisor and the advisor included as co-author; mere submission is not accepted and co-first authorship is not recognised.

Doctoral publication requirement: both (1) at least one SCI(E)-level journal paper published or accepted and (2) at least one international conference paper or domestic journal paper published or accepted, or at least one registered international patent; the advisor must be a co-author and the student must be first author excluding the advisor.
Doctoral students admitted before 2008 need only one SCI(E)-level paper.
Proof of publication or acceptance (for example, an acceptance email) must be obtainable before the result documents deadline.
Students who have completed coursework must register as graduate research students.

Before the thesis submission period (4 years for master's, 6 years for doctoral after completion) expires, completers must apply for an extension of the submission period or register as research students beyond the period; contact the department office.
Students who withdrew from thesis examination last semester must repeat every step from the online application this semester.
To cancel after applying online, email the department office.
Application is complete only after both the online application and submission of documents to the department office.
For doctoral students, if a foreign national with no affiliation in Korea is appointed as an external examiner, additional documents are required; contact the department office.
Only the '2026 Seoul National University Human Rights/Gender Equality Education' certificate is accepted.
Since Spring 2026, the advisor's recommendation letter (master's and doctoral) and the doctoral CV are no longer required.
The doctoral thesis examination request form requires the advisor's confirming signature.
Doctoral students whose examination period extension was approved last semester are exempt from the examination fee.
Master's students who submit the thesis for examination directly to committee members must inform the department office by email.
Students who cannot meet the result documents deadline for unavoidable reasons must contact the department office before the deadline.
Doctoral students must hold two examinations (first and final); the first examination may be closed to the public.

Doctoral students must book the examination room themselves; if the date or room of the public first examination changes, they must email the department office in advance and post a notice of the change on the door of the original room.

Thesis non-disclosure (up to 3 years) is allowed only for (1) a domestic or international patent application (filed or planned), (2) military secrets, or (3) a confidentiality agreement with a company, with supporting documents and the advisor's approval; journal publication is not an accepted reason.
Extension of the examination period is for doctoral students only and is allowed only once; it cannot be renewed if already extended last semester.

Students postponing graduation by not submitting the archival thesis must have passed the examination and met the publication requirement, must submit result documents this semester, must register as research students next semester and must check their thesis submission deadline.
Students who extend or withdraw must register as research students next semester and check their thesis submission deadline.
If the final thesis is not submitted, the degree cannot be awarded; no submission or correction is possible after the library deadline.
Only PDF files are accepted for the final thesis; no bound copy is submitted.
The approval page must bear signatures or seals; for every committee member whose signature is a copy, evidence of approval (such as an email) must be submitted.

Students who did not submit the archival thesis or who extended the doctoral examination last semester and graduate this semester must use submission and approval dates within this semester, not last semester.

The publication date on the outer cover must be February 2027; the submission date on the approval page is the year and month of the thesis-for-examination deadline and the approval date is the year and month of the final examination deadline.
The final thesis title, the title in the library upload file and the title on the approval page must be identical.
Abstract keywords must be within 7 to 8 words.
Students must comply with SNU's Research Integrity Committee Regulations, Research Ethics Guidelines and AI Guidelines.
steps: All applicants: Read the Fall 2026 degree conferral regulations post (https://ece.snu.ac.kr/community/academics?md=v&bbsidx=57963), the completion self-diagnosis checklist in the FAQ post and the academic handbook, and confirm you meet all eligibility requirements; also read the attachments (their content was not read for this translation).

All applicants: Between 21 September and 1 October 2026, 17:00, apply online on the department intranet (https://ece.snu.ac.kr/intranet/): register your official SNU email, tick your advisor's field as sub-major (Biomedical Engineering: tick 'Bio' [바이오]), tick the examination fee box, mark all SNU professors as internal members [위원(교내)], and enter full personal details (including bank account and resident registration numbers) for any external examiner.

Master's students: By 1 October 2026, 17:00, submit to the department office (Building 301, Room 319): master's thesis examination application (printout of the application page), committee recommendation form (attachment), external examiner details (application page printout) and bank transfer form (attachment) if you have an external examiner, research ethics compliance form (attachment), and the 2026 SNU Human Rights/Gender Equality Education certificate (https://helplms.snu.ac.kr > 나의강의실 > 수료증발급(국문)).

Doctoral students: By 1 October 2026, 17:00, submit to the department office (Building 301, Room 319): doctoral thesis examination request form with your advisor's signature (application page printout), committee recommendation form (application page printout), external examiner details (application page printout) and bank transfer form (attachment), research ethics compliance form (attachment), and the 2026 SNU Human Rights/Gender Equality Education certificate (https://helplms.snu.ac.kr > 나의강의실 > 수료증발급(국문)).

All applicants: Between 21 October and 3 November 2026, 17:00, pay the examination fee via MySNU > 학사정보 > 졸업 > 논문관련 > 논문심사료 납부고지서, by transfer to the virtual account or directly at the designated bank (exempt if your doctoral examination extension was approved last semester).

Master's students: In November 2026 (date to be announced), write [master's, student ID, name, committee professors' names] in pencil at the bottom right of the first page of each copy and submit the thesis for examination to the department office (Building 301, Room 319); if you give copies directly to committee members, inform the office by email.
Doctoral students: Book your examination room and deliver the thesis for examination directly to all five committee professors at least one week before your presentation.
All applicants: Collect examination refreshments from the department office (Building 301, Room 319) before your examination day, allowing spare time as stock may run out.

Master's students: At the public presentation (November, schedule to be announced by email), fill in your details on the thesis examination summary form (attachment) and hand it directly to the committee chair before you start.

Doctoral students: At the public first examination (November, schedule to be announced by email), fill in your details on the result table, examination summary, oral examination score sheets and ballots (attachment) and hand them directly to the committee chair before you start; then hold the final examination.

Master's students: By 14 December 2026, 17:00, submit to the department office: master's thesis examination summary (1 copy); proof of publication or acceptance; a copy of the paper's first page highlighting your name, your advisor's name and the conference or journal name; for conferences, proof of publication or acceptance (and of presentation if given); Korean abstract (1 copy); English abstract (1 copy).

Doctoral students: By 21 December 2026, 17:00, submit to the department office: examination result table (1), examination summary (1), oral examination score sheets (5), ballots (5), outstanding thesis award recommendation (only if applicable), preliminary examination result report (1), publication documents for the SCI(E) paper and for the conference paper, domestic journal paper or patent (first-page copy or patent proof highlighting your name, advisor's name and venue name, plus acceptance proof, and presentation proof for conferences if presented), Korean abstract (1), English abstract (1), and doctoral journal achievement checklist (1).

All applicants: If applicable, submit a committee member change request (and, for external examiners, their details and bank transfer form) before your public presentation; submit withdrawal or extension documents, or the statement for not submitting the archival thesis, by 14 December, 17:00 after contacting the office; and submit a non-disclosure request form with evidence by 8 January 2027, 17:00.

All applicants: Between 15 January and 1 February 2027, 23:59, upload the final thesis including the approval page as a PDF to the library, following the forthcoming Fall 2026 final thesis submission notice (refer to last semester's notice until then).

All applicants: Between 15 January and 22 January 2027, 17:00, submit the thesis submission confirmation form and the original signed or sealed approval page to the department office (Building 301, Room 319).
translation:
★Fall 2026 Graduate Thesis Examination Schedule

※ The content of this notice may change later, so please check it regularly.

1. [Eligibility to apply for thesis examination]

1) Pass in the thesis qualifying examination: foreign language + major examination
- Students taking the thesis qualifying examination in Fall 2026 should apply first and, if they fail, contact the department office to cancel.
- Even if you passed the major examination, you cannot print the fee bill if you failed the foreign language subject (you can check this in MySNU > 학사정보 > 졸업 > 졸업시험 신청 > 종합시험 판정결과 조회).
- Since Spring 2006, the English subject of the qualifying examination has been replaced by a certification system. Students concerned (those not already recognised as passing) must obtain a TEPS or TOEFL score at or above the threshold set by the College of Engineering and submit the score to the department office before submitting thesis examination documents (by early March or early September each semester).

2) Meeting the completion requirements
- The SNU completion simulator does not reflect department rules and is therefore not accurate. You must read the completion self-diagnosis checklist in the [FAQ] post and the academic handbook and check whether you have completed the program.
- If you do not meet the completion requirements, graduation will not be possible regardless of whether you pass the thesis examination. Be sure to check with the self-diagnosis checklist before the examination.

3) Meeting the degree conferral (publication) requirements
* You must read the post on the regulations applicable to Fall 2026: https://ece.snu.ac.kr/community/academics?md=v&bbsidx=57963
※ Conference publications for which only an abstract is submitted are eligible if the conference has a peer review process. Have the publication confirmed by your preliminary examination committee and submit the signed confirmation form before the result documents deadline. The confirming signature may be obtained after the preliminary examination. For detailed criteria and the confirmation form, see the notice on the changed degree conferral regulations.

Master's: Submit documents proving that at least one domestic or international conference paper or domestic or international journal paper has been published or accepted. Your name must be first among the authors excluding the advisor, and the advisor must be included as a co-author. Proof such as the publication record or acceptance email must be obtainable before the result documents deadline; mere submission is not accepted.
- Co-first authorship is not recognised for master's students.

Doctoral: Only papers or patents that include the advisor as co-author and list the degree candidate first among the authors excluding the advisor are recognised. Both (1) and (2) must be met:
(1) At least one paper published or accepted in an internationally recognised journal (SCI(E) level).
(2) At least one international conference paper or domestic journal paper published or accepted, or at least one registered international patent.
※ Proof for (1) and (2), such as the publication record or acceptance email, must be obtainable before the result documents deadline.
- Eligible for doctoral thesis examination (first and final examination): those who passed the preliminary examination last semester.
- Notice 'List of conferences recognised as SCI(E)-level international journals': related notice (link in the original notice).
- Notice on recognition of co-first authorship: related notice (link in the original notice).
- Admitted before 2008: one SCI(E)-level paper / strengthened from 2008 admissions: (1) one SCI(E)-level paper + (2) one international conference paper, domestic journal paper or registered international patent.

4) Students registered as research students / students whose thesis submission period has not expired
- Students who have completed coursework must register as graduate research students.
- 4 years for master's and 6 years for doctoral after completion (does not apply to enrolled students; applies only to completers).
- Just before this period expires, you must apply for an extension of the thesis submission period or register as a research student beyond the period (see the related notice, linked in the original, and contact the office).

2. [Fall 2026 thesis examination schedule]
1. Online application and submission of application documents: 21 September 2026 (Mon) to 1 October 2026 (Thu), 17:00
2. Payment of thesis examination fee: 21 October 2026 (Wed) to 3 November 2026 (Tue), 17:00
3. Submission of thesis for examination: scheduled for November 2026
4. Submission of thesis examination result documents: Master's: by 14 December 2026 (Mon), 17:00; Doctoral: by 21 December 2026 (Mon), 17:00
* If you need an extension of the result documents deadline for unavoidable reasons, contact the office separately (advance contact before the deadline is required).
5. Final thesis submission (including the approval page [인준지] and thesis submission confirmation form [학위논문제출확인서]); if not submitted, the degree cannot be awarded: 15 January 2027 (Fri) to 1 February 2027 (Mon), 23:59
6. Request for approval of thesis non-disclosure: after the examination ends until 8 January 2027 (Fri), 17:00

3. [Fall 2026 thesis examination details]★

1) Online application and submission of application documents
- Deadline: 21 September 2026 (Mon) to 1 October 2026 (Thu), 17:00
(Notes)
- Students who withdrew from thesis examination last semester must go through every step of the thesis examination this semester, starting from the online application.
- If you wish to cancel after applying online, contact the office by email.
- For committee member eligibility, see the attachment and the rules on thesis committee composition (related notice linked in the original).
- Submission method: the application is complete only after both (a) the online application (department intranet, https://ece.snu.ac.kr/intranet/) and (b) submission of documents to the department office.

(a) Online application instructions
- Email: register your official SNU email. All examination notices will be sent to your SNU email, so be sure to check it.
- Sub-major: tick your advisor's field. Reference page linked in the original notice. (Biomedical Engineering: tick 'Bio' [바이오].)
- Payment confirmation: when submitting the application, tick the thesis examination fee box for now.
- Committee information: tick 'member (internal)' [위원(교내)] for all SNU professors.
- External examiners: personal information (including bank account number and resident registration number) is required. Refer to the attachment and enter accurate information.

(b) Documents to submit to the department office
Master's:
1. Master's thesis examination application: printout of the application page
2. Thesis committee recommendation form: printout of the attachment
3. (If you have an external examiner) external examiner's personal details (printout of the application page) and bank transfer request form (printout of the attachment)
4. Research ethics compliance confirmation: printout of the attachment
5. Human rights/gender equality education certificate (only the '2026 Seoul National University Human Rights/Gender Equality Education' certificate is accepted)
- https://helplms.snu.ac.kr > 나의강의실 > 수료증발급(국문)

Doctoral:
1. Doctoral thesis examination request form: printout of the application page
2. Thesis committee recommendation form: printout of the application page
3. External examiner documents: external examiner's personal details (printout of the application page) and bank transfer request form (printout of the attachment)
- If a foreign national with no affiliation in Korea is appointed as an external examiner, additional documents are required; contact the office.
4. Research ethics compliance confirmation: see the attachment
5. Human rights/gender equality education certificate (only the '2026 Seoul National University Human Rights/Gender Equality Education' certificate is accepted)
- https://helplms.snu.ac.kr > 나의강의실 > 수료증발급(국문)

※ As the regulations and guidelines on simplifying master's and doctoral thesis examination application documents have been revised, the advisor's recommendation letter for master's and doctoral theses and the doctoral CV have been removed from the required documents from Spring 2026.

2) Payment of thesis examination fee
- Deadline: 21 October 2026 (Wed) to 3 November 2026 (Tue), 17:00
- Method: MySNU > 학사정보 > 졸업 > 논문관련 > 논문심사료 납부고지서 > transfer to the virtual account, or pay directly at the designated bank.
※ Virtual account payment is possible from 21 October 2026 (Wed), 09:00 to 3 November (Tue), 17:00; on weekdays during the payment period you can pay 24 hours a day (closes at 17:00 on the last day).
- Students whose doctoral thesis examination period extension was approved in the previous semester are exempt from payment.

3) Submission of thesis for examination
- Who: master's students (doctoral students should deliver it directly to all five professors at least one week before the presentation).
- Deadline: scheduled for November 2026
- Method: write [master's, student ID, name, names of committee professors] in pencil at the bottom right of the first page of each copy and submit to the office.
※ If you submit individually to committee members, inform the office by email.
- Content: this is the thesis submitted before the examination; submit the thesis as written so far. No set binding format.

4) Submission of thesis examination result documents
Master's: by 14 December 2026 (Mon), 17:00
* If you need an extension of the deadline for unavoidable reasons, contact the office separately (advance contact before the deadline is required).
1. Master's thesis examination summary, 1 copy
2. Publication documents:
1) Documents proving that at least one domestic or international conference paper or domestic or international journal paper, with your name first among the authors excluding the advisor, has been published or accepted (mere submission and co-first authorship not accepted)
- Recognised as a conference or journal paper only if the advisor is included in the author list (e.g. the part of the conference program book showing your name, publication confirmation, acceptance email)
2) Copy of the first page of the paper, 1 copy (highlighting required: your name / advisor's name / conference (or journal) name)
3) For conferences, proof of publication or acceptance (including proof of presentation if the presentation has taken place)
3. Korean abstract, 1 copy
4. English abstract, 1 copy

Doctoral: by 21 December 2026 (Mon), 17:00
* If you need an extension of the deadline for unavoidable reasons, contact the office separately (advance contact before the deadline is required).
1. Doctoral thesis examination result table, 1 copy
2. Doctoral thesis examination summary, 1 copy
3. Oral examination score sheets, 5 copies
4. Ballots, 5 copies
5. Recommendation for the outstanding doctoral thesis award, 1 copy [only if applicable]
6. Doctoral thesis preliminary examination result report, 1 copy
- Example: a. preliminary examination schedule / b. first examination (or preliminary examination) schedule / c. first examination (or blank) schedule / d. blank (or first examination) 4. preferred date and time of final examination
7. Publication documents:
(1) SCI(E)-level journal
- Copy of the first page of the published paper, 1 copy (highlighting required: your name / advisor's name / conference (or journal) name)
- Proof of publication or acceptance, such as an acceptance email
(2) International conference, domestic journal or registered international patent
- Copy of the first page of the paper or patent proof, 1 copy (highlighting required: your name / advisor's name / conference (or journal) name)
- Proof of publication or acceptance, such as an acceptance email or publication record
- For international conferences, proof of publication or acceptance (including proof of presentation if the presentation has taken place)
8. Korean abstract, 1 copy
9. English abstract, 1 copy
10. Doctoral journal publication checklist, 1 copy

Only where applicable:
1. Students withdrawing from or extending the examination
- Must submit documents by 14 December (Mon), 17:00, referring to the attachment (advance contact with the office required).
2. Change of thesis committee members
- Submit the committee member change request form before the public presentation date (see attachment).
- If changing an external examiner, also submit the external examiner's personal details and bank transfer request form.
3. Request for approval of thesis non-disclosure (up to 3 years)
- Submit the thesis non-disclosure application form (see attachment).
- Supporting documents are required, and it is possible only in one of three cases: (1) (domestic or international) patent application (filed or planned), (2) military secrets, (3) a confidentiality agreement signed with a company.
- Advisor approval is required; simple journal publication is not accepted.
4. Students not submitting the archival thesis
- Submit a statement of reasons for not submitting the archival thesis by 14 December (Mon), 17:00 (see attachment).
- This is for students who passed the examination and met the publication requirement and are postponing graduation by one semester, so the result documents must be submitted this semester.
5. Three ways to postpone graduation by one semester (see attachment)
1. Not submitting the archival thesis (passed examination + publication requirement met) — Master's: yes; Doctoral: yes. Result documents must be submitted this semester; research student registration next semester is required; you must check your thesis submission deadline.
2. Extension of the examination period (see attachment) — Master's: no; Doctoral: yes. Can be extended only once; cannot be extended again if extended in the previous semester; research student registration next semester is required; you must check your thesis submission deadline.
3. Withdrawal from the examination (see attachment) — Master's: yes; Doctoral: yes. Research student registration next semester is required; you must check your thesis submission deadline.

5) Final thesis (approval page) submission
1) Final submission of the thesis (approval page) to the library
- Period: 15 January 2027 (Fri) to 1 February 2027 (Mon), 23:59 ★No submission or correction is possible after the deadline, so submit with time to spare.
- Only the original file is submitted online, without a bound copy (only PDF can be uploaded).
- Details will be posted in the Fall 2026 final approved thesis (archival thesis) submission notice (refer to last semester's notice for now).
2) Final submission of the thesis (approval page) to the department office
- Period: 15 January 2027 (Fri) to 22 January 2027 (Fri), 17:00
- Documents: (1) thesis submission confirmation form [학위논문 제출 확인서], (2) approval page [인준지] (original)

[How to prepare the thesis (approval page)]
1. Signature or seal on the approval page is required.
- If a signature is a copy, you must submit evidence (e.g. email) confirming the committee member's approval (evidence is needed for every member whose signature is a copy).
2. If last semester's 'students not submitting the archival thesis' or '(doctoral) examination period extension applicants' graduate this semester, the submission date and approval date must be within this semester. Last semester's dates are not allowed.
3. Approval page form: see attachment.
4. How to write it: see attachment. Write February 2027 as the publication date on the outer cover.
- On the approval page, write as the submission date the year and month in which the thesis-for-examination deadline set in the examination plan falls, and as the approval date the year and month in which the final examination deadline falls. For detailed examples, check this semester's thesis writing guide.
5. The final thesis title, the thesis title in the file uploaded to the library and the thesis title on the approval page must be identical.

4. [Thesis presentation schedule and refreshments]
1) Master's public thesis presentation
- Schedule: November (a schedule survey will be sent by email soon, followed by a notice).
- Document required before the presentation starts: fill in the thesis examination summary (attachment – result documents) yourself (department, student ID, name, thesis title, etc.) and hand it directly to the committee chair.
- Each examination lasts 25 minutes in total: a 15-minute presentation, and 10 minutes for questions and evaluation, clearing the room and changeover to the next presenter.
2) Doctoral public thesis presentation (first examination)
- Schedule: November (a schedule survey will be sent by email soon, followed by a notice).
- Documents required before the presentation starts: fill in the thesis examination result table, examination summary, oral examination score sheets, ballots, etc. (attachment – result documents) yourself (department, student ID, name, thesis title, etc.) and hand them directly to the committee chair.
- Book the examination room yourself.
- The first examination date is a guideline; you may present privately and may hold it after the end of November. However, you must hold two examinations in total: the first and the final examination.
- Seminar students audit doctoral first examinations (public presentations), so if the date or room changes, be sure to inform the office by email in advance. (Post a notice of the new date and room on the door of the original room.)
3) Examination refreshments
- Applicants will be informed by email.
- Collect refreshments from the department office (Building 301, Room 319) before the examination date (items may run out temporarily, so allow spare time before your examination).

5. [Other]
- Guide to the thesis similarity check program [new] (see attachment).
- Check and comply with SNU's Research Integrity Committee Regulations, Research Ethics Guidelines and AI Guidelines.
- Enquiries: department office (Building 301, Room 319); the staff contact details are given in the original notice.

Notes on completing the attached forms
Abstract keywords must be within 7 to 8 words, according to this semester's thesis writing guide.
Thesis non-disclosure requests are accepted only for reasons in the College of Engineering thesis examination plan; the journal publication reason shown in the example on the common form is not accepted.
The doctoral thesis examination request form requires the advisor's confirming signature.
